JHS Pedals browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal JHS Pedals The Hard Drive - Modern Distortion Published on June 29, 2024 JHS Pedals distortion pedal Black Black Tan Tan Information The JHS Pedals Hard Drive is a high-gain distortion pedal developed as an original circuit, marking the company's first design not derived from an existing topology. The concept originated in 2016 with the goal of capturing the high-gain guitar tones associated with 1990s and early 2000s post-grunge and alternative rock. Rather than adapting established pedal or amplifier circuits, the design process shifted toward a ground-up approach, resulting in a finalized product after approximately eight years of development. The internal architecture is based on cascaded gain stages combined with a hard limiting circuit, followed by a Class AB amplifier section. This signal path feeds an active tone-shaping network consisting of a sweepable midrange control and Baxandall bass and treble controls. The equalization system allows adjustment of both the level and the selected frequency range of the mid band, enabling detailed shaping of midrange response. The circuit is intended to produce a wide range of distortion textures, from lower-gain, tube amp-style crunch to dense, high-gain saturation suitable for cutting through stage or studio mixes. The Hard Drive holds significance as the final completed design by JHS head engineer Cliff Smith, whose work on the circuit was finalized shortly before his passing in 2021. The project reflects an extended period of experimentation focused on complex gain staging and achieving a tube-like response using solid-state circuitry. Controls Volume : Controls the overall output level of the pedal. Mid Freq : Selects the frequency range affected by the midrange control. Drive (Distortion) : Adjusts the amount of distortion gain. Bass : Adjusts low-frequency response; center position is flat. Middle : Adjusts midrange level; interacts with the Mid Freq control to determine affected frequencies. Treble : Adjusts high-frequency response; center position is flat. Footswitch : Silent soft-touch switching with buffered bypass. In 2016, Josh had the idea to develop a circuit that covered the best high-gain distortion tones of the ’90s and 2000s, a sound that embodied the post-grunge alternative rock movement. We started by looking at pedals, then amps, and after exploring the typical paths of circuitry, we took a sharp turn and started from scratch. Eight years later, the pedal is finished and ready to take you to the next level. The Hard Drive goes harder and further than any gain or distortion we’ve released so far. A FRESH APPROACH A fresh approach to achieving high gain distortion in a pedal format, the Hard Drive includes cascaded gain stages and a hard limiting circuit, followed by a class AB amplifier section that drives a “sweepable midrange” EQ and Baxandall bass and treble controls. With its generous external controls, the Hard Drive lets you dial in everything from grinding tube amp crunch to a bona fide wall of distortion that can easily cut through any stage or studio mix. HONORING CLIFF SMITH The Hard Drive holds a special place in JHS history as the final design work of our former head engineer, Cliff Smith. The prototype and design had been finalized just weeks before he passed away in 2021. “I don't know that there's ever been a JHS circuit where we experimented more. It was always a loose and casual approach to getting this right. I knew something great would come of it, so we just let it simmer…Cliff would call the Hard Drive circuit a mutt, and I agree– meaning this circuit is not a clone of anything in particular but rather an original iteration of tons of different inspirations and ideas, kind of like the Colour Box that he and I developed years earlier. I have vivid memories of Cliff spending entire weekends and nights tinkering and experimenting with this circuit. He would message me notes on the weekend when he got excited about something he stumbled into. This pedal was his hobby for a long time.
